We walked without talking past the signs for $0.59 chicken legs and the crates of oranges, under the elevated, straight to the water. The Hudson was gray, the light was gray. I couldn’t shake the refrigerator’s chill, and the humidity made it worse. Claude pulled a pack of cigarettes out of her back pocket and struggled to light one—she must have been more shook up than she let on. She flipped her lighter shut and let the dud cigarette dangle from her lips. “So, no shit, huh.”


I had only one thought: “We gotta go back there and do something.”


“Do what.”


“Free them. It’ll take a while to do each cage manually, but I don’t know what else we can do.”


She stuck the unlit cigarette behind her ear. “And then what?”


I felt a shift between us, like someone had let the air out.

actions.what: Claude 把语气放软，先问「What is this doing to you, Renata?」，Renata 反问「你是什么意思」；Claude 说明自己是受过训练、拿钱办事的人，反问 Renata 把自己整个打开去吸收这些是在做什么；Renata 想把话拉回「这不是关于我」，Claude 顶回去：你不能揣着那样东西还说自己没事。

She asked, softer, “What is this doing to you, Renata?”


“What do you mean?”


“I get paid for what I do. I got trained. But you, you just go around absorbing all that? Do you know what you’re doing?”


“It’s not about me, we gotta—”


“You can’t hold something like that and tell me you’re okay.

actions.what: Renata 低头看浑浊的河水（想着「掉进去太容易了」）并问「你看见他了吗」；Claude 侧过头答「我不知道我看到了什么」，并说自己不是在否认——只是不知道看到的是什么；Renata 庆幸她没否认，认定 Claude 确实招呼过他、感到过他在，只是我们最依赖的那一样感官（sight）给不出她能信的答案；她心里生出「也许我来教她」。

I looked down at the murky river. It would be so easy to fall in. “Did you see him?”


“I don’t know what I saw.” She looked at me askance, and then said, “I’m not denying…but I don’t know what I saw.”


I was glad she wasn’t denying it. And I knew that she had addressed him, felt him, knew he was there, even if her sight, that one singular sense that we rely so heavily on, didn’t tell her something she could trust. Maybe I’d teach her.

actions.what: Renata 肯定她「在里面时知道该怎么做」；Claude 说她只是跟那人讲了话——有人正在难过，就试着把他讲通（她再次试着点烟；Renata 想替她把双手稳住，但看来她不想被碰）。Claude 自己接着往下说：若他是带着目的回来的倒还好，可他只是「Leftover」、像没地方可去；她连着喊了两声 Lord，做了一个像要画十字的手势又收回。

I said, “You knew exactly what to do in there.”


“I just talked to the guy. That’s what you do if someone’s having a tough time, you try and talk ’em through.” She tried to light her cigarette again. I wanted to put my hands over hers to steady them, but it didn’t seem like she wanted to be touched.


She went on. “It’d be one thing if he was back for a purpose, you know? He was just…I don’t know what he was. Leftover. Like he had no place to go. Lord,” she said, exhaling. “Lord.” She made a quick gesture like she was about to cross herself and then thought better of it.

I tried to put myself in her shoes. I tried to remember how I felt the first time I saw a ghost. “I know that the first encounter with a ghost can be—”


“Uh-uh. You’re not listening. I don’t know about ghosts. I’m telling you that I can’t deal with the dead. I can’t help them. I don’t know how to do that. I help the living. That’s what I do.”


“But you have to agree it’s real.”


She snorted. “I see people die every day. Every goddamned day.

I wasn’t angry at her—I didn’t feel anything but empty—but I couldn’t help my words from coming out salty. “Didn’t you take an oath to help people?”


“To those in my care, yes.” She finally got her cigarette to light and took a deep drag. She exhaled slowly. “You have no idea what my days are like. We opened a new ward on the dirtiest floor of our oldest, shittiest building. It’s already packed.

I kicked a beer bottle into the river. “I just want to get them out. It’s like a fucking jail. It doesn’t have to be an emotional investment, it’s just—”


“Emotional? Honey, I’m talking about my body. I’m talking about my peace of mind. I’m tired.”


“I know, I know, I can’t imagine how hard—”


“No, you don’t know.” She stopped walking and faced me. “It’s impossible to treat this thing. It affects every damn system of the body all at once. All day, we’re throwing shit at the wall to see what sticks. I got guys minutes from death asking to be intubated. Yesterday, I had to decide if I should give this guy a drug that might kill him immediately or help him live a few more weeks, but I thought, He’s gonna die anyway, so may as well! Do you understand what I’m saying? It’s not just weighing on me emotionally. I’m talking about the work.”


I put my hand on her arm tentatively. I felt her relax just slightly, and then I put my arm around her. “I want you to tell me about it.”


“It feels better to just let it go when I’m off the clock,” she said quietly. “Seven p.m. comes around, I leave it at the door. Isn’t there any kind of way you can do the same? You burn out otherwise.

actions.what: Renata 抢在对方之前把拒绝替她说出口（「你不想帮，行，我明白」）——那不是她想说的；她希望自己更勇敢、能按她的条件与她相处，但必须保住自己以免彻底绝望；她顺势宣告自己大概会忙不过来、不会在她眼前出现。Claude 回头问「It’s like that, huh?」，Renata 只回「It is what it is.」。Claude 先给她一个硬眼神（脑中闪过性，被她抖掉）后神色变软——Renata 看出她在为自己难过；Claude 把一只手搭上她肩膀，留下「You survive it. I’ve dealt with this pain, and you survive it.」；两人再无话说，Renata 在感到她的手移开之前就知道她已经走了；转身时她已过了那条公路——她没回头——Renata 等她从视野里消失，然后向东走，离开河边。
actions.anchor:
You don’t want to help, all right. I understand.” It’s not what I wanted to say, but that’s what I said. I wished I was a little bit braver and could meet her on her terms, but I needed to hold on to myself or I’d risk total desperation. “I’ll have my hands full, probably, so you won’t see me around.”


She turned back to me. “It’s like that, huh?”


It hurt, but I felt like if I did anything more than shrug, I’d die on the spot. “It is what it is.”


She gave me a hard look—sex flicked across my brain but I shook it off—before her face softened. She was feeling sorry for me. I turned back toward the river and felt a hand on my shoulder. I couldn’t turn around to look at her, but I heard what she said. “You survive it. I’ve dealt with this pain, and you survive it.”


Neither of us said anything more. I knew she was gone before I felt her hand move.


I turned around and she was already across the highway. I waited until she disappeared from my sight—she didn’t look back—before making my way east, away from the river.
